sections.h2: Why the county line matters in Draper
sections.html:
About 20 miles south of Salt Lake City, Draper straddles two counties, Salt Lake and Utah. The city covers roughly 30 square miles at an elevation of 4,751 feet, right where the Salt Lake Valley narrows into Utah Valley at the Point of the Mountain.

That line decides who assesses your house, who mails the bill and where the deed gets filed. Schools split along it as well, with Canyons on the Salt Lake County side and Alpine on the Utah County side. Look at the parcel number on your tax notice first. Neighbors a few blocks apart can answer to different offices, calendars and school boundaries.

Draper had 51,017 residents in 2020, up from 7,257 in 1990. Many neighborhoods were built in that window, so houses range from old farm lots to subdivisions less than a generation old. The median home value is $784,800, median gross rent is $1,894, and 68.6% of homes are owner-occupied. That leaves roughly 31% rented, so if you are selling a rental, the tenant situation matters as much as the building.

Foothill homes are most exposed. The city council adopted Ordinance 1695 in December 2025, which adds a Wildland Urban Interface Area to city code. Boundaries and rules are not spelled out in the public notice, so request the full ordinance from the city if your lot backs onto open hillside.

A separate state program adds another layer. Utah House Bill 48 of 2025 led the state forestry division to publish a wildfire risk map scoring each building from 1 to 8. A building that scores 7 or higher and sits within 250 meters of at least two other buildings falls inside the high-risk boundary, and its owner may owe the state an annual fee once the program starts, which the state expected later in 2026.

  • Enter your address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov ahead of listing or answering an offer.
  • Save a printed score to hand over with the contract.
  • Ask city planning whether the lot lies in the new interface area.

Two approvals are required to host short stays in Draper: a business license and a short-term rental permit. Short term means under 30 consecutive days, with a two-night minimum, and the permit renews yearly. A day of unpermitted hosting is a separate violation each time.

Accessory dwelling units have separate limits.

  • A detached ADU needs a residential lot of at least 12,000 square feet.
  • An internal ADU generally needs a residential lot over 6,000 square feet on a qualifying street, and the city has mapped areas where internal units are banned.
  • The owner must live in the main dwelling for both types.
  • ADU rentals must run at least 30 consecutive days, and each needs one extra on-site parking space.

Basement apartments built without permits are a frequent problem. Owners who skipped the February 1, 2022 application window face immediate enforcement, and a buyer relying on a loan may balk. Draper's planning office answers questions at (801) 576-6399.

In both counties the state exempts 45% of a primary residence, so tax falls on 55% of market value. A rental home can qualify as a primary residence under state rules. A vacation home cannot.

Property tax timing for each side of Draper
Parcel inTax noticesDue datePenalty on December 1
Salt Lake CountyValuation notices July 22, tax notices by November 1November 30Greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel
Utah CountyThird week of OctoberNovember 30Greater of 1% or $10

Salt Lake County's Board of Equalization hears valuation appeals from August 1 to September 15. Should a notice arrive while your house is listed, pass it to the title officer so closing handles that year's bill properly.

Selling for cash is an ordinary Utah closing with the lender removed.

  1. Give us the address and describe tenants, liens and repairs.
  2. We review the property against nearby recent sales.
  3. The offer is yours to take or turn down.
  4. A title company searches title and drafts the closing documents.
  5. The county recorder for your parcel files the deed.

Filing costs little. Salt Lake County takes a flat $40 per recording, and Utah County's standard fee is the same $40 per document. In Salt Lake County the deed also needs a notary acknowledgment, the grantee's address and the tax serial number. The title company works out the closing date with you.

Begin with the parcel number and latest tax notice, which show the county that applies. Add any ADU permit or application receipt, your short-term rental permit and renewal date, the wildfire score printout and your loan payoff figures, plus the lease if a tenant lives there.

Wildfire paperwork deserves its own line in that folder. The state map can change how a buyer sees a foothill house, and the annual fee tied to high-risk buildings is not yet in place. Showing the score upfront, along with what you know about defensible space around the house, keeps the conversation factual.

Giving the title officer this folder at the outset cuts the back-and-forth that drags out many closings. A buyer also sees what the house may and may not be used for before signing.

Five problems recur.

  • A hillside lot with a high state wildfire score.
  • An older basement unit with no ADU permit.
  • A short-term rental permit that lapsed after its annual renewal.
  • A tenant in place on a rental.
  • Confusion over whether the parcel is billed by Salt Lake County or Utah County.

Order matters here: sort out the county first, then permits, then the wildfire score. Each answer shapes the next conversation with a buyer or the title office.

Rentals add another wrinkle. With roughly 31% of occupied homes not owner-occupied, many Draper buyers expect to see lease terms, so have the dates, rent and deposit ready if a tenant is in the house.

All can be solved, yet each adds steps to a conventional listing. Selling directly lets the house go as it stands, with paperwork sorted at the title company.

Part of the Silicon Slopes tech corridor, Draper reports more than 1,000 businesses. Interstate 15 crosses town, TRAX Blue Line trains stop at Draper Town Center and Kimballs Lane, and FrontRunner has a station here. Two airports, Salt Lake International and Provo Municipal, are about 30 minutes away. Tech workers and rail commuters often ask how far a house is from the stations.

faqs.q: Is Draper in Salt Lake County or Utah County?
faqs.a: Both. Which county handles your bill and deed depends on the parcel, and the number on your tax notice tells you.

faqs.q: When are Draper property taxes due?
faqs.a: In both counties the deadline is November 30, shifting to the next business day when it lands on a weekend or holiday.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Draper house short term?
faqs.a: Yes. You need a business license and a short-term rental permit, renewed annually. Every day without both is its own violation.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Draper house that has an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes, though buyers will ask. An ADU permit comes before any rental, and the owner must live in the main dwelling. Cash buyers can take the house as is. Financed buyers may want the permit settled first.

faqs.q: How do I check wildfire risk for a Draper address?
faqs.a: Type it in at wildfirerisk.utah.gov to get a score from 1 to 8. A building scoring 7 or higher near other buildings counts as high risk.
